content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels the Luke 2:48-49 comparison UNDERDETERMINED because the single verse's \"thy father\" is qualified by \"my Father's business,\" which is the kind of single-verse ambiguity K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"\"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand\": reading (a) Luke 2:48-49's \"thy father\" and \"my Father's business\" are two senses that both stand, so the comparison cannot be UNDERDETERMINED on that basis; reading (b) the second phrase qualifies the first and leaves the single verse open. I weighed (a) against (b).","why":"The judge text treats a single verse's two-sense/qualified wording as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, while K-S2 requires both senses to stand and forbids single-verse ambiguity from making the matter open."}
